item.title: Iran declares it has won the war as U.S. turns to economic warfare
item.description: Iran's president said Friday the world had "approved" the country's victory, as Vice President JD Vance declares economic pressure "the most effective tool that we have."

item.title: Russian strike on Ukraine kills at least 2, a day after deadly mall attack
item.description: The attack comes after a two-wave drone strike on a shopping mall in Zelenskyy's home town mall killed 16 people.

item.title: U.S. set to impose 50% tariffs on Canada after failed talks; Canada to match them
item.description: The U.S. was set to impose 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian products early Saturday. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney countered that Canada would match them "dollar for dollar."

item.title: Drastic water cuts issued for California, Nevada and Arizona from Colorado River
item.description: Federal officials announced sharp water cuts for the next two years on Friday for three Western states that rely on the imperiled Colorado River.

item.title: She was a California comeback story, serving juvenile probation in a UC Davis dorm for killing a teen, when arrested again
item.description: A Sacramento County judge ordered her into a UC Davis program for formerly incarcerated students. She was arrested seven months later, accused of dealing drugs from her dorm, where officers found ammunition.

item.title: Pilot reports possible burn injuries after passenger's laptop catches fire
item.description: "I think we have about four to five passengers that were burned by the laptop," a pilot can be heard saying in air traffic control audio obtained by CBS News.

item.title: Men describe being deported by U.S. to dangerous African nation: "We cannot leave"
item.description: The Central African Republic is one of more than 30 countries the U.S. government has convinced to accept third-country deportees arrested as part of President Trump's large-scale crackdown on illegal immigration.

item.title: Trump threatens defamation suit against left-leaning think tank
item.description: President Trump's legal team is threatening to sue left-leaning think tank Center for American Progress for defamation over a report it issued that found "no evidence that National Guard deployments have reduced violent crime."

item.title: Trump campaigns with Darline Graham in South Carolina ahead of runoff
item.description: Sen. Darline Graham is facing Rep. Ralph Norman to replace her late brother on the ballot in November.

item.title: NFL storylines as preseason hits Week 2
item.description: Jacob Robinson, staff writer for the Athletic, joins CBS News to discuss the biggest headlines in the NFL as the league gears up for the regular season.

item.title: Some "third country" U.S. deportees refused to get off plane in Liberia
item.description: The western African nation of Liberia has received the first round of "third country" deportees from the United States. The plane with roughly 20 deportees landed on Thursday. U.S. officials tell CBS News some of the passengers refused to deboard upon landing. The Trump administration has brokered deals with at least 35 countries to deport people to places where they have no ties. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez reports.

item.title: Powerful storms bring record rainfall, tornadoes across U.S.
item.description: Violent storms are bringing multiple tornadoes and record rainfall across the East Coast and beyond. Jared Ochacher reports.

item.title: Psychiatrist who helped get Andrea Yates acquitted testifies in Clancy trial
item.description: Dr. Phillip Resnick, whose testimony contributed to an acquittal in another high-profile child-killing case in 2001, testified in Lindsay Clancy's defense on Friday. Shanelle Kaul has more.

item.title: The roller coaster popularity of plastic surgery
item.description: A new piece in The Free Press looks at the roller coaster popularity of plastic surgery. Freya India, author of the report and contributing writer for the Free Press, joins CBS News to discuss. The Free Press is a Paramount publication.

item.title: Another child's room now a silent memorial to the toll of school shootings
item.description: In south Minneapolis, a second-floor bedroom remains much as it was. For the parents of 8-year-old Fletcher Merkel, it's something every American should see.

item.title: Inside the bedroom of a little boy killed in the Minneapolis Annunciation church shooting
item.description: It's been a year since a shooting at Annunciation Catholic Church in Minneapolis killed two children and injured dozens. Steve Hartman visits the bedroom of a little boy who lost his life that day.

item.title: Hayden Panettiere was given Narcan after being found unconcious, witness says
item.description: New details in Hayden Panettiere's sudden death have emerged as her on-and-off boyfriend's brother, who was present when she died, speaks out. Mark Strassmann has more.

item.title: Flock camera sabotage grows amid privacy concerns
item.description: Cities across the country are unplugging Flock cameras used to record traffic and other violations as privacy concerns grow. Jason Allen has more.

item.title: Russian strike kills 15 people at shopping mall in Zelenskyy's hometown
item.description: Zelenskyy described the attack as a double-tap strike, in which an initial wave of drones hit the area, followed by a second wave as rescue workers responded.

item.title: Pentagon moves to fire publisher and editor of Stars and Stripes
item.description: The Pentagon has given separation notices to both the publisher and the editor-in-chief of Stars and Stripes, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Trump administration deports immigrants to dangerous Central African Republic
item.description: Camilo Montoya-Galvez speaks to two men who were deported to the dangerous Central African Republic instead of their homes.

item.title: Reports of sexual assault in U.S. military declined for third straight year
item.description: The review included data from an anonymous survey conducted every other year that asks service members whether they've been the victim of unwanted sexual conduct or harassment.

item.title: Body of New York grandmother who went missing in Las Vegas found, sister says
item.description: The body of Alisa Goods, a New York grandmother who went missing while visiting Las Vegas, has been found after more than a week, her sister told CBS News' Alice Gainer.

item.title: 8/21: CBS Evening News
item.description: Psychiatrist testifies in Clancy trial; Powerful storms rock East Coast.

item.title: Supreme Court temporarily allows work on White House ballroom to continue
item.description: Chief Justice John Roberts issued a stay that will remain in place until the Supreme Court takes further action.

item.title: People are scrambling to find wads of cash dropped all over American cities
item.description: Cash drop social media accounts have people racing to find money hidden across the country. Here's what's behind the viral videos.

item.title: Woman covertly filmed by Meta smart glasses raises privacy concerns
item.description: One woman is speaking out after she was secretly filmed, saying that technology like Meta's AI-powered smart glasses threatens personal privacy.

item.title: AI companies accused of hoarding and destroying millions of books
item.description: Consumer advocates are urging the FTC to examine whether AI developers are hurting competition and reducing public access to source material.

item.title: Cardiac event reveals Olympian's rare heart condition: "There was a God present"
item.description: Olympian Jenny Simpson said she won't be able to run again after being diagnosed with a rare heart condition earlier this year.

item.title: Appeals court reverses former paramedics' convictions in McClain death
item.description: The Colorado Court of Appeals reversed the criminally negligent homicide convictions for the former paramedics in the death of Elijah McClain.
